questions.q: What does a variable in Power Automate give you that a plain dynamic content value does not?
options: A value you can change and build on as the flow continues running
A faster connection to the trigger's source app
Automatic translation of the value into other languages
A value that persists permanently across every future run of the flow
questions.explain: Dynamic content is fixed once an action produces it. A variable is something you create and can update repeatedly as the flow runs, but it only exists for that one run.

questions.q: Which three fields does the Initialize variable action require or accept?
options: Connector, Trigger, and Condition
Name, Type, and an optional Value
Scope, Loop, and Index
Subject, Body, and Recipient
questions.explain: Initialize variable takes a Name, a Type (String, Integer, Float, Boolean, Array, or Object), and an optional starting Value.

questions.q: Why can't you place an Initialize variable action inside an Apply to each loop?
options: Loops don't support any actions at all
Variables can only be declared at the flow's top level, not inside loops, conditions, or scopes
It would run too slowly inside a loop
Apply to each only accepts connector actions, not built-in actions
questions.explain: Initialize variable is restricted to the top level of the flow. To change a variable's value inside a loop or condition, initialize it beforehand and use Set variable inside the loop instead.

questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics wants to count how many shipments get flagged for manual review as a loop processes each one. Which action should go inside the loop to update that count?
options: Initialize variable
Append to array variable
Increment variable
Set variable, with the value hardcoded to 1
questions.explain: Increment variable adds a number (default 1) to an existing Integer or Float variable each time it runs, which is exactly how a running count is built across loop iterations.

questions.q: A flow needs to build up a growing list of flagged shipment IDs as it loops through requests. Which action adds a new value onto the end of an existing array variable without overwriting what's already there?
options: Set variable
Append to array variable
Increment variable
Initialize variable, called again for each item
questions.explain: Append to array variable inserts a new value as the last item in an existing array, which is how a list grows across iterations. Set variable would replace the whole array instead.
